title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
description: Monotonic increasing stack of indices. When a shorter bar arrives, pop and compute the rectangle whose height is the popped bar; its width spans from the new stack-top to the current index. Append a 0 sentinel so everything drains at the end.

notes: Stack stores INDICES with strictly increasing heights — that lets you derive width on pop.
Width on pop: if the stack is empty, the popped bar extends from 0 to i (width = i). Otherwise width = i - newTop - 1.
Append a 0 sentinel to the heights array so the final stretch of increasing bars also gets popped and measured.
Each index is pushed and popped at most once → O(n) amortized.

options: Indices whose heights are strictly increasing

questions.q: When you pop index `top` and the stack is non-empty, the rectangle width is:
questions.explain: The popped bar extends from just after the new stack top to just before i.

questions.q: Why append a 0 to the end of heights?
options: To force the stack to drain so trailing bars are measured
It is required by the problem

exercises.prompt: Fill in the monotonic-stack histogram solver.

blanks.hint: remove and read the top index
stack empty → bar extends from 0 to i

L3.prompt: Write `largestRectangleArea(heights)` returning the area of the largest rectangle. Use a monotonic stack with a 0 sentinel. Log `largestRectangleArea([2, 1, 5, 6, 2, 3])`.
hints: Keep a stack of indices with strictly increasing heights.
When a shorter bar arrives, pop and measure: width = stack empty ? i : i - newTop - 1.
Append a 0 sentinel so the final increasing run still pops.
